facts.statement: Navajodactylus is an extinct genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico.
facts.quote: Navajodactylus (meaning "Navajo finger") is an extinct genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from Late Cretaceous (late Campanian stage) deposits of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico, United States.

facts.statement: Oceanographer Arjan C. Boeré discovered and collected the holotype specimen of Navajodactylus from the Kirtland Formation in 2002.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Navajodactylus was discovered and collected by oceanographer Arjan C. Boeré from the Kirtland Formation in 2002.

facts.statement: Robert M. Sullivan and Denver W. Fowler named the genus Navajodactylus in 2011, with Navajodactylus boerei as the type species.
facts.quote: Navajodactylus was first named by Robert M. Sullivan and Denver W. Fowler in 2011 and the type species is Navajodactylus boerei.

facts.statement: The generic name Navajodactylus honors the Navajo Nation by combining their name with the Greek word for finger.
facts.quote: The generic name honors the Navajo Nation, combining their name with a Greek δάκτυλος, daktylos, "finger".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to the upper Campanian stage, approximately 75 million years ago.
facts.quote: Navajodactylus is based on the holotype SMP VP-1445, from the Hunter Wash Member of the Kirtland Formation, San Juan Basin, dating to the upper Campanian, about 75 million years old.

facts.statement: A paratype specimen consists of an ulna fragment.
facts.quote: The paratype is SMP VP-1853, an ulna fragment.

facts.statement: Specimens from Alberta were initially referred to Navajodactylus but were later reassigned to the genus Cryodrakon in 2019.
facts.quote: Two first phalanges, TMP 72.1.1 and TMP 82.19.295, both from the Dinosaur Park Formation of the Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta, were referred to this taxon, but in 2019, Hone et al. recognized these as referable to their new azhdarchid Cryodrakon.

facts.statement: Navajodactylus was tentatively placed in the family Azhdarchidae based on its age, but it lacks defining shared characteristics of that group.
facts.quote: Navajodactylus was tentatively assigned to the family Azhdarchidae because of its geological age, however, it does not show any synapomorphies of the group.

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether Navajodactylus is truly an azhdarchid because it lacks the extensive air pockets in its forelimb bones typical of that family.
facts.quote: Indeed, it may not actually be an azhdarchid, as it lacks pneumacy in its forelimb elements, which is opposed to the extensive pneumacy seen in azhdarchids.

facts.statement: Navajodactylus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The holotype consists of three pieces of the first phalanx of the wing finger.
rejected.quote: It consists of three pieces of the first phalanx of the wing finger.

rejected.statement: Navajodactylus was a medium-sized pterosaur with an estimated wingspan of 3.5 meters.
rejected.quote: Navajodactylus was a medium-sized pterosaur, with an estimated wingspan of 3.5 meters (11.5 ft).
